chosen.title: The Deadline That Moved: How Industry Lobbied the EU Into Delaying Its Own AI Law
chosen.rationale: On August 2, 2026 the EU AI Act's high-risk obligations were supposed to bite; instead an 'Omnibus' deal quietly pushed stand-alone Annex III compliance to December 2027 and embedded-product rules to 2028 after heavy corporate pressure — even as 75% of the public wants stronger AI rules. That gap between who asked for the delay and who wanted the guardrails is exactly Dawn's follow-the-money, name-the-capture territory.

sources.name: Gibson Dunn — EU AI Act Omnibus Agreement: Postponed High-Risk Deadlines
CIGI — The Great Digital Disconnect: AI Deregulation Versus Public Trust
Holland & Knight — U.S. Companies Face EU AI Act's August 2026 Deadline

rejected_candidates.title: Nobody Is Liable: The Chatbot Death Settlements and the Accountability Void in Engineered Intimacy
rejected_candidates.rationale: Google and Character.AI just moved to settle five lawsuits — including the wrongful-death case of 14-year-old Sewell Setzer III — over companion chatbots engineered to form emotional bonds with minors and marketed without age checks or crisis safeguards. A quiet mediated settlement lets the product's designers pay their way out of a public reckoning; Dawn's beat is precisely who gets harmed, who profits, and why the accountability never lands.

sources.name: K-12 Dive — Character.AI, Google agree to mediate settlements in wrongful teen death lawsuits
TechPolicy.Press — Lawsuits Exposed How Chatbots Endanger Children. Can the Senate's New Bills Fix It?

rejected_candidates.title: Nudify Nation: The AI Sexual-Deepfake Industry and the Platforms That Let It Run
rejected_candidates.rationale: Regulators are now formally sanctioning platforms over synthetic sexual imagery — Canada's Privacy Commissioner found X in breach of consent law for generating sexualized deepfakes — while 'nudify' apps industrialize image-based abuse that falls overwhelmingly on women and girls. This is the gendered, image-based-abuse story the 'deepfakes and democracy' framing keeps missing, and it's squarely Dawn's feminist-and-postcolonial critique of who technology claims to serve versus who it targets.
